source.context: Educational walkthrough for students showing complete two-operation machining workflow on a 5-axis CNC machine

features.door: interlocked safety door (must be locked to cycle start)

features: IIT logo (engraved on back, programmed in Mastercam as subprogram)

first_operation.description: Machine the back/bottom face and external contour from raw stock

probing_steps: Renishaw ruby-tip probe touches points in X and Y
Establishes center point of raw stock material
Rectangular measurement for exact center of material
work_offset_setup.probing_rationale: Raw stock from saw has variation (0.060-0.125 inch), so probing finds true center each time - operator does not need to precisely position stock, just center it by eye in vise

workholding.method: Part clamped on vise teeth (no parallels for first operation)

torque_wrench.method: Torque wrench clicks when correct clamping force is reached

notes: No dead blow hammer needed for first op (would damage teeth)
Part centered by eye in vise - probe finds exact center
One hand holding camera, normally would use two hands to position and clamp

machining_sequence.details: Block center cycle to find X/Y center, edge measurement for Z0, writes to G510 work offset
machining_sequence.notes: Run probe at 100% rapid for accuracy

machining_sequence.details: Face mill with X and Y extents defined, machine to Z depth
machining_sequence.notes: Turn coolant off initially to verify Z0 contact, then turn coolant on

machining_sequence.details: Contour around rectangular profile - roughing pass, two Z-level passes
machining_sequence.notes: Check gap between tool tip and vise top with a scale/ruler before allowing full contour pass

machining_sequence.details: Finishing contour pass using same geometry as roughing
machining_sequence.notes: Do not change feed override during finishing pass to avoid inconsistent surface finish

machining_sequence.details: Chamfer edges using same geometry as rectangular spigot
Calls subprogram 98420 (Mastercam-generated G-code for complex logo toolpath)
machining_sequence.notes: Logo too complex for hand-written G-code or conversational programming

first_operation.simulation: Always simulate program in ShopMill before running on machine

second_operation.description: Flip part over to machine the top face, pockets, holes, and final features

work_offset_setup.method: Work stop (fixed reference) - no need to re-probe each part

adjustment_technique.measurement: Use height gauge on surface plate to verify Z dimension
adjustment_technique.first_part_measured: 0.725 on one side, 0.726 on other side
adjustment_technique.tolerance_check: Within +/- 0.003 tolerance but want to be more accurate
adjustment_technique.offset_correction: Subtract 0.0005 inches (half a tenth) from Z offset for next part
adjustment_technique.note: Split the difference: measured 0.0005-0.001 over nominal, took off half a tenth

part_orientation.flip_method: Flip part over (top-to-bottom) keeping lettering/numbering oriented correctly
part_orientation.correct_flip: Flip like a page (about the long axis)
part_orientation.incorrect_flip: Do NOT flip end-over-end (about the short axis)
part_orientation.registration: Part pushed against work stop for consistent positioning

workholding.type: Machine vise with parallels and work stop
workholding.parallels: Used for second operation (part sits on parallels for Z reference)
workholding.work_stop: Fixed reference so XYZ zeros don't need re-establishing each part

seating_technique.pattern: Alternating corners like changing a tire lug pattern
seating_technique.sequence: Corner 1, Corner 2 (opposite), Corner 3, Corner 4, then center (5th)
seating_technique.purpose: Seat part firmly on parallels - parallels should not be loose after seating

notes: Parallels must be checked - if loose after clamping, need dead blow hammer
Always check parallels didn't move after first operation (during unload)

machining_sequence.details: Face the top surface to establish Z datum for second operation features
machining_sequence.notes: Turn off coolant to verify Z0 contact, ease in with feed override
Check gap between tool and vise with scale before full pass
Modified drill point used to combine drilling with chamfer/deburring to avoid a third operation

deburring_strategy.problem: Second operation left burrs at two hole locations
deburring_strategy.solution: Modified drill point to deburr during drilling - avoids third operation setup
deburring_strategy.verification: Feel by hand for high points, re-run drill if burr remains

measurements.status: Within +/- 0.003 tolerance, adjusted offset for next part

steps: Load program in ShopMill program manager
Verify correct machine block for correct part number
Run 3D simulation to visually verify toolpaths match blueprint
Select 'Execute' to load program to machine control
Start with both rapid and linear feed override pots turned all the way down (0%)
Hit cycle start - machine will prompt for feed
Turn up rapid ONLY to allow tool change to cycle
Turn rapid back down after tool change completes
Turn up rapid slowly to allow approach to workpiece
When program switches from G00 (rapid) to G01 (linear), switch from rapid pot to linear pot
Ease linear feed in slowly to see first contact with workpiece
Turn off coolant during initial approach to visually verify Z0 contact
After confirming good Z0 contact, turn coolant on
Cycle stop (interrupt) program after first pass to physically check tool-to-vise clearance with a scale/ruler
If gap exists between tool tip and vise top, safe to continue
Resume with cycle start after verification
safety_rules: ALWAYS keep a hand near E-stop or Cycle Stop button
ALWAYS wear safety glasses when opening door
Do NOT increase feed override during a finishing pass (causes inconsistent surface finish)
Verify tool won't cut into vise jaws before allowing full contour pass
Use distance-to-go display on controller to monitor remaining travel

after_first_part_verified: Run at 100% rapid and 100% linear feed
Adjust work offset as needed based on measurements
Track dimensions trending toward tolerance limits
part_handling: Use 3D-printed part holders to prevent scratching between stacked parts
Blow off coolant and chips with air gun before removing part
Check parallels haven't moved when removing part from vise

work_offset_adjustment_technique.method: Subtract (or add) measured deviation from Z value in work offset table

example.adjustment: Subtracted 0.0005 (half a tenth) from G543 Z offset
example.rationale: Split the difference since both sides measured slightly different

Each program block shows conversational icons (roughing, finishing, etc.)
Execute button loads program to machine
M6 tool change runs in background during ShopMill execution

probing.purpose: Work offset establishment - find center of stock and Z0

face_mill.purpose: Face milling top surface of stock

key_manufacturing_insights.topic: Probing eliminates manual touch-off for varying stock
key_manufacturing_insights.detail: When raw stock is saw-cut with variation up to 1/8 inch, using a probe cycle to find the true center eliminates the need for precision stock or manual indication. The operator just eyeball-centers the stock in the vise.

key_manufacturing_insights.topic: Work stop for second operation repeatability
key_manufacturing_insights.detail: A fixed work stop eliminates the need to re-probe or re-establish work offsets for each part in second operation. Part just pushes against the stop for consistent registration.
Use alternating-corner pattern (like lug nuts on a tire) when seating part on parallels: corners 1-2-3-4 then center. This ensures even seating and tight parallels.
Always start first run with both pots at zero. Turn up only the pot needed for current G-code mode (rapid for G00, linear for G01). This gives full operator control over approach speed.

Before allowing a full contour pass, interrupt the program and slide a steel scale between the tool tip and vise top. Any visible gap confirms safe clearance. This is the most practical way to verify the tool won't crash into the vise.
Turn off coolant during first approach so you can see and hear the tool make contact with the workpiece. This confirms Z0 is correct before committing to the cut.
Never change feed override during a finishing pass. Changing the feed mid-pass will create visible surface finish variation from one side of the part to the other.

After measuring first part, adjust work offset by splitting the difference of the oversize amount. Example: part measures 0.001 over on one side, 0.0005 over on other - subtract 0.0005 from Z offset for next part.
Complex toolpaths like logos are better programmed in CAM software (Mastercam) and called as subprograms from the main ShopMill conversational program. Don't try to hand-code complex contours.
A modified drill point can both drill and deburr holes in one operation, eliminating the need for a separate third setup operation. Verify by feel with finger across hole.
When flipping part for second operation, maintain consistent orientation relative to engraving/features. Flip about the correct axis to ensure features align with program expectations.
Always run the ShopMill 3D simulation and compare to the physical blueprint before executing a program. The simulation gives a visual sanity check even though you can't pull dimensions from it.
Using a torque wrench set to 75 newton-meters ensures consistent clamping force across all parts in a production run. The click indicates proper force is reached - do not over-tighten.

The controller's distance-to-go display shows remaining travel in the current block. Use this to anticipate when the tool will reach the workpiece and when to switch between rapid and linear feed control.
